name: Sara Balloo's Plea
summary: Sara Balloo's Plea is a handwritten missive penned by a grieving widow in Ironforge. Unable to face the monarch directly in her sorrow, she entrusts this letter to a trusted champion of the Alliance to carry before King Magni Bronzebeard.

sections.title: A Widow's Appeal
sections.body: Written in the shadow of deep personal tragedy, Sara Balloo's Plea represents a humble appeal directly to Ironforge's throne. Rather than braving the High Seat herself in her grief-stricken condition, Sara seeks an adventurer who has demonstrated loyalty and valor to the Alliance to deliver her words. The message asks for the attention of King Magni Bronzebeard, drawing the sovereign's gaze toward the private mourning and sacrifices made by ordinary dwarven families serving the kingdom.

faq.answer: It is a handwritten letter penned by Sara Balloo, addressed to King Magni Bronzebeard, asking for his royal attention while she mourns in private.

faq.q: Why does Sara Balloo need someone else to deliver it?
faq.answer: Sara feels overcome with grief and believes appearing before the King of Ironforge in such an emotional state would hinder her plea, prompting her to rely on an Alliance champion instead.
The letter is addressed and delivered directly to King Magni Bronzebeard in the High Seat of Ironforge.

faq.q: What does delivering the letter lead to?
faq.answer: Presenting the letter to King Magni draws his attention to Sara Balloo's bereavement and initiates a royal response honoring her fallen family.

angles.text: For dwarves, carrying Sara's message to the High Seat is an act of deep kinship, ensuring that even in grief, no mountaineer or citizen goes unheard by King Magni.
Sara entrusts her petition only to champions recognized for their service to the Alliance, trusting their reputation to grant her appeal an audience before royalty.
